comments.author: @luckydelauta3859
comments.text: Back in the mid-1980s I was on my way from Guam to Palau, with what was supposed to be a quick stop in Yap. The engines on the Continental Air Micronesia jet should have been left on while we boarded a few new passengers. However, one of the cockpit crew inadvertently or accidentally shut them down and they could not be restarted because of a faulty APU (starter). So, everyone had to deplane while Continental radioed back to Guam for help. I ended up getting a room at the hotel which was owned by Continental in Colonia, the Capitol. With nothing to do for several hours, I hired a car to take us on a tour. By "us", I mean me and the 3 flight attendants who were also stuck there. We saw lots of stone money and bare chested women, not to mention the thousands of red splotches of betel nut which routinely get spit out  on the ground everywhere. When we finally were able to leave, I remember the local man who was checking our documents before reboarding the plane. He had the biggest smile and the shiniest dark red teeth (almost ebony colored) stained from years of chewing betel nut.  It was an inconvenient stop, but turned into a fun little adventure.

replies.author: @BeyondTravel7777
replies.text: Talk about turning an annoying flight delay into an unforgettable adventure! Being stuck in Yap back in the day and just rolling with it to explore the island is such a cool piece of personal history.
